articleTitle: Evaluating the Optimal Power Flow Impact on Power Network Areas with the Dynamic State of Voltage Stability in Multi-Machine Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: A new algorithm to evaluate the dynamic state of voltage stability in multi-machine power systems is presented in this paper. Non-linear programming is applied to determine the optimal power flows using the gradient search technique. The results of the optimal simulation of the generator output powers are analyzed to determine the impact on the dynamic voltage state in the multi-machine power system. A mathematical model of the area transient voltage stability criteria is proposed, allowing the evaluation of the dynamic voltage state caused by the sudden short circuit fault that changes the structure of the multi-machine power systems, consisting of several power network areas containing several load buses. Power network areas have different values of transient voltage stability criteria to be evaluated. This new algorithm evaluates the dynamic voltage states, considering the impact of automatic voltage and frequency regulations in multi-machine power systems. The nonlinearity of the power network is mathematically simulated due to the change in angular velocity of the generator over time. Examples and results in this paper will typically illustrate the advantages of this new algorithm proposed with the area transient voltage stability criterion formula.

articleTitle: Power Loss and Efficiency Calculation of a Power Conversion System (PCS) for EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive power loss and efficiency calculation of the Power Conversion System (PCS) for a hypothetical Electric Vehicle (EV) charging station. The PCS, which connects the grid and the EV, comprises six push-pull converters and one inverter. The loss calculation focuses on the conduction and switching losses in the semiconductor devices within PCS. Afterward, the efficiency of the individual converters and overall PCS is calculated. The calculation reveals that an individual push-pull converter and inverter exhibited a total power loss of 56.7W and 26.5W, while the overall PCS power loss became 366.7W. The calculation also reveals that the push-pull converter and inverter have 84% and 98% efficiency, respectively. Due to the lower efficiency of the push-pull converter, the PCS efficiency significantly reduces and becomes 95%. Finally, this paper concludes that a new topology for the PCS of an EV charging station is imperative for optimum performance, thus, beneficial for the EV industry.

articleTitle: Industrial mechanical equipment failure prediction based on Transformer-CLS
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Mechanical equipment, serving as the backbone of manufacturing, is crucial to every aspect of industrial production. During its operation, mechanical equipment inevitably encounters issues like wear and tear, leading to a variety of malfunctions that escalate over time, thereby impacting production quality and efficiency. This study presents a visual analysis of the operational and failure data of mechanical equipment. We integrates conventional machine learning techniques with advanced deep learning algorithms to forecast failures. The model’s performance is assessed using metrics such as the confusion matrix, ROC curve, precision, and recall. The paper concludes by affirming the efficacy and advantages of the Transformer-CLS model in predicting failures of industrial mechanical equipment. This approach demonstrates a marked enhancement in the precision and recall rates of failure predictions compared to traditional models, alongside notable transfer learning capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on hardware-in-the-loop simulation of static var generator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In light of the issue that the grid’s high reactive power consumption and the reduction in power quality brought about by the addition of new energy power generation both contribute to some degree of grid voltage fluctuation. And the requirements of model parameter testing cannot be satisfied by the current detecting device. Research approach for static variable generator (SVG) hardware-in-the-loop system optimization using Simulink is proposed. Initially, the SVG control mechanism and mathematical model are suggested. Next, using Simulink, SVG modeling and control methods are investigated in accordance with the real requirements of power system simulation, and the model’s operational outcomes are examined to confirm its dependability. Lastly, SVG hardware-in-the-loop simulation testing was carried out using the PXI real-time simulator and StarSim HIL software. The model’s dependability and accuracy have been confirmed, and it is better able to satisfy the demands of real power system modeling applications.

articleTitle: Analytical Power Loss Model for GaN Transistors Based on Temperature and Parasitic Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The emergence of wide bandgap power devices based on Gallium Nitride (GaN) material has propelled the development of power electronic converters towards high frequency, high power density, and miniaturization. However, as switching speed increases, so does the proportion of switching losses. Accurate analysis of switching loss is crucial for evaluating and optimizing converter performance, as well as enhancing system reliability. This paper establishes a comprehensive GaN device switching loss model that considers parasitic parameters and temperature effects. The impact of key parasitic parameters on GaN devices is analyzed, and the switching losses using an analytical model that considers the relationship between device parasitic capacitance, PCB parasitic parameters, temperature variations, and losses is estimated. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified on a double pulse experimental platform based on GS66516T. Extensive experimental results show that under different working conditions and temperatures, the error between the proposed loss model predictions and actual losses remains within 10%, thus enabling accurate prediction.

articleTitle: Stoichiometric Ratio Optimization in Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells: Impact on Performance and Polarization Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In the present experimental study, a single Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cell (PEFC) was tested to investigate the effect of changing stoichiometric ratios on cell performance. For this purpose, a test bench with a control system consisting of a mass flow, temperature, and relative humidity controller was used, configured through specialized software for fuel cell testing. A current sweep was applied, and the response values were automatically collected via a data acquisition system connected to the cell. The results indicate that a higher Stoichiometry ratio (SR) does not necessarily imply better cell performance, as it was found that the ratios of $\mathbf{1. 7 5}$ for the anode and 2.5 for the cathode optimized the voltage-power response of the cell in a range evaluated from 1.0 to 3.0 of SR. Furthermore, it was found that the variation of SR on the cathode side strongly impacts activation resistance at low current densities, while ohmic and concentration resistances were affected by relative humidity on the anode side when varying the SR. These findings are of great importance because obtaining optimal stoichiometric ratios minimizes voltage losses, leading to more efficient use of the reactive gases in a PEFC. This is particularly significant in the transportation sector, where there is a high projection of PEFC usage.

articleTitle: The Technological Disruption Caused by the Composite Insulator Crossarm in the High Voltage Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The newest disruptive technology in the high voltage transmission system is the use of composite materials in the towers. This includes composite insulator crossarms. The possibility on reduction of towers, clearances, compaction of the lines, and so on, makes this new technology very attractive to transmission lines designers. The use of such tower design changes the infrastructure, and the usuals technical requirements and has several impacts on the supply chain of this sector. This technology eliminates the problem of bird droppings on insulator string.

articleTitle: Research on Power Quality of Critical Loads of Electric Springs Based on Quasi-PR Dual Closed-loop Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of the strategy for dual PI closed-loop control in the grid voltage fluctuation, voltage at the critical load in the Electric Spring (ES) system has the steady state error as well as the high harmonic content, this paper introduced the quasi-PR controller into the second generation of the Electric Spring (ES-2), and researched a strategy for dual closed-loop control utilizing the quasi-PR controller for both the external voltage loop and the internal current loop. The working process of this control strategy is introduced, the control loop is designed, and the stability of the electric spring system based on the quasi-PR controller is analyzed. Through simulation comparison with the control strategy for dual PI controllers on the MATLAB/Simulink platform, it is verified that the strategy for dual closed-loop control with quasi-PR controllers can better stabilize voltage at the critical load and suppress the harmonics on voltage at the critical load during the fluctuation of the grid voltage.

articleTitle: Electrolyzers Parameters Impacting Alkaline Water Electrolysis Hydrogen Production
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The study examines the behavior of alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) when altering electrodes thickness, spacing, and roughness. In addition, the study examines the effects of heating the electrode using induction heater. Increasing electrodes’ thickness improves the AWE efficiency by reducing electrical resistance losses, while it increases $A W E$ cell weight. The study has found that the optimum electrodes spacing for given design is around 5 mm. In addition, increasing electrode roughness from $0.95 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ um to $1.96 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ has increased cell efficiency from 54% to $\mathbf{6 2 \%}$. The results showed that induction heating of electrodes has improved AWE cell efficiency by 8% while causing slight increase in the cell temperature.

articleTitle: Development and Installation of an Independent Energy Supply for Civil Defence and Disaster Control: Chances and Challenges for “InES-CDDC“
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The number of extreme weather events and natural disasters is increasing. In additional to food and medical care people need drinking water and electrical energy to survive and to reconstruct the infrastructure. A student project of the Bochum University of Applied Sciences is therefore developing a mobile independent supply system with which people can be optimally supplied with drinking water and energy. In this paper the authors describe the status of development, the functions of the individual modules as well as the requirements and challenges for a stand-alone system like this.

articleTitle: Short-term wind power prediction based on a CEEMDAN-SSA-LSTM-Attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Accurate wind power prediction facilitates power system operation, peak regulation, security analysis, and energy conservation and reduction. In this paper, we propose a short-term prediction model for wind power based on a Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN)-Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA)-Attention Mechanism-Long Short Term Memory Neural Network (LSTM). Firstly, the wind power signal is decomposed into multiple sub-sequences using CEEMDAN. Secondly, in order to improve the accuracy of wind power prediction, the SSA algorithm hyperparameter optimized LSTM is applied to extract the timing features, and the Attention mechanism is introduced to strengthen the attention of the important information in time-series inputs. Finally, a wind power plant in Guangdong, China, is selected to analyze its operation data in 2021. Simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the wind power prediction error and improve the prediction accuracy compared with other methods.

Author Keywords: Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN)
Attention Mechanism Long Short Term Memory neural network (Attention LSTM)

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Logic Controller Design in An Off-grid Microgrid with Hydrogen Production
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper presents a fuzzy logic control approach for an off-grid microgrid with a long-term hydrogen production system. Fuzzy logic control utilizes fuzzification, membership function design, fuzzy control rule formulation, and defuzzification to achieve energy regulation of energy storage systems. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the fuzzy logic control approach in achieving optimal power management, longer lifespan of lithium battery, and maintaining system stability.

articleTitle: The Energy Management and Planning of the Proposed Water-Energy Nexus Concept by Considering Tidal Turbine and INVELOX as Novel Options
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The energy and water crisis due to the rapidly growing population and developing societies caused countries and governments to think about novel technologies and ways to respond to this issue. Therefore, this paper is about energy planning and management of the proposed concept for supplying water and energy simultaneously. This approach helps to overcome and supply the dramatic energy need of desalination and distribution systems. This article aims to supply the demands and minimize the total cost at the same time. Various renewable and non-renewable energy resources such as tidal turbines, INVELOX turbines, CHP, micro-turbines, and other elements are utilized in the proposed planning. Real weather conditions are considered to compute the output power of wind and tidal turbines. The presented water-energy nexus structure is modeled as a MINLP concept and solved in GAMS software using various solvers to illustrate the reliability of the optimization answers. The final results show a high improvement in the total cost reduction.

articleTitle: A Simplified Average Magnetizing Current Control for DC-DC Current-Source Soft-Switching Solid-State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified average magnetizing current control for a DC-DC current-source soft-switching solid-state transformer (S4T). The current-source S4T has a small size, full-range soft-switching, controlled $d v / d t$, and no electrolytic capacitors. However, its magnetizing inductance acts as a reduced DC link, leading to low inertia and high magnetizing current ripple. The existing PI control requires the integration of magnetizing current. Therefore, it requires a 400 kHz sampling frequency, significant computational resources, and high-speed FPGA and DSP controllers. For this reason, a simplified average magnetizing current control is proposed. First, it uses the average magnetizing current as a control variable, samples at the beginning of the resonant state, and calculates the average magnetizing current as a feedback value. Second, since the magnetizing current varies linearly, the integral term can be simplified as the product of the average magnetizing current and the dwelling time of the active state, omitting the integration and continuous comparison process. The proposed method reduces the sampling frequency to the switching frequency of 18 kHz while simplifying the calculation. Simulation results show that the proposed method can operate stably under steady state and load step, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: USB-C/A Charger with GaN FET
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In this project we successfully designed a 65-Watt (W) USB-C and USB-A outlet charger for portable devices. The specifications for the charger are listed in Table II below. The difference with our charger compared to others in the market is the use of a Gallium Nitride (GaN) Field-Effect Transistor (FET) to process the switching conversion in the AC-DC conversion instead of a typical Silicon transistor. In this paper we will discuss the background of GaN transistors as well as the advantages of lower on-state drain to source resistance (Rds(on)) and parasitic capacitances that lead to improved efficiency. Then we will discuss the basic circuit topology of the 65W USB charger and the results of efficiency with the GaN FET used.

articleTitle: Integration of C2000 Microcontrollers with MATLAB Simulink Embedded Coder: A Real-Time Control Application
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: C2000 ${ }^{\text {TM }}$ 32-bit microcontrollers excel in real-time control, optimizing closed-loop performance for various applications such as industrial motor drives, solar inverters, digital power systems, and sensing. The lineup offers Premium and Entry-performance microcontroller units (MCUs). This paper explores the integration process of Texas Instruments ${ }^{\text {TM }}$ (TI) C2000 microcontroller units with MATLAB and Simulink using Code Composer Studio (CCS) and Embedded Coder (EC) support package for C2000 microcontrollers. It shows how to set up Simulink to program the Digital Signal Processor (DSP) microcontroller unit and the communication between the host computer and the C2000 target hardware using the LAUNCHXLF28379D launchpad. Basic functions such as Pulse Width Modulation, Analog Digital Conversion, and Proportional-Integral controllers are explained. Finally, a closed-loop control model for a C2000 Digital Power Buck Converter BoosterPack is implemented, showcasing the effective integration of TI C2000 microcontroller units with MATLAB, Simulink, and related tools for real-time control in the power system context.

articleTitle: Steady-State Fault Analysis of Distribution System with PV Plants and EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The fundamental nature of the distribution system (DS) is changing with the mix of electromagnetic-based components (e.g., rotating machine sources and transformers) interacting with newer switched-mode-based sustainable energy technologies. As distributed energy resources (DERs) such as solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, battery storage, and electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure penetrate into the DS, the way faults behave will change. This paper conducts an analysis of how the fault levels are affected by integrating various scenarios of PV plants and EV charging stations. A network model of a real distribution system in Oklahoma is implemented in OpenDSS software. The simulations are conducted for the various capacities of a central PV plant, single-phase residential PV plants, and EV charging stations. The results of each simulation case and the comparison of fault levels of the DS with a single central PV plant, residential PV plants, and EV charging stations are discussed.

articleTitle: Seamless Switching Control Strategy from Grid-Connected to Islanded Mode for Shunt-Type Dynamic Voltage Regulator Under Nonlinear Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: With the escalating number of sensitive electrical apparatus within the grid, the adverse effects of voltage sags have become increasingly apparent, driving the rapid development of research on shunt-type dynamic voltage regulator (S-DVR). Given that S-DVR has two independent operating modes, namely grid-connected and islanded mode, the significance of effective switching control strategies becomes particularly pronounced. However, considering that the current research on switching control strategies is mostly based on linear loads, this paper proposes a seamless cut-in control strategy from grid-connected to islanded mode applicable to nonlinear loads. The proposed control strategy ensures seamless switching at the control strategy level while achieving rapid turn-off of triodes for alternating current (TRIACs), reaching the purpose of seamless switching from grid-connected to islanded mode with satisfactory control effect. The effectiveness of the proposed seamless cut-in control strategy is confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: Transformer Neural Networks for Intrusion Diagnostic Unit (IDU) and Anomaly Detection in Distributed Energy Resources (DERs)
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Modern critical infrastructure such as an electric grid, uses information and communication technologies (ICT) to increase system performance. However, the integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and their interconnectedness to ICTs exposes them to different threat landscapes. To defend and mitigate cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure, there is a critical need for robust situational awareness tool(s) and strategies. This paper reviews the existing work on the deployment of Transformer Neural Networks (TNN) in Intrusion Detection Units (IDUs) and Anomaly Detection (AD) applications. Additionally, the paper discusses specific stealthy attack scenarios and provides recommendations by mapping Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, and Accountability (CIAA) properties to different attacks. To realize a resilient electric grid, authors suggest DER stakeholders to carefully review IEEE 1547.3-2023 standard recommendations.

articleTitle: Component-level cost analysis of aqueous organic redox flow batteries: An island case study from Canada
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This research investigates the economic viability of redox flow batteries using organic molecules for sustainable energy storage, focusing on the synthesis costs and environmental impacts. We propose that replacing vanadium with electroactive organic molecules can offer significant economic advantages. Despite their scalability and flexibility, the adoption of these batteries is hindered by high synthesis costs of organic molecules, which have a short lifespan. By refining synthesis methods and exploring alternative raw materials, costs can be reduced, simplifying manufacturing processes and shortening supply chains. A case study on the Magdalen Islands (Îles-de-laMadeleine) electricity grid in Quebec, Canada, extrapolates grid-level energy storage costs based on component-level cost information of a new battery prototype. Results suggest these costs are feasible within public utility budgets. This research contributes valuable insights for decision-makers and stakeholders in the energy sector, facilitating informed decisions for transitioning towards environmentally friendly energy technologies.

articleTitle: Optimization of PMa-SynRM torque characteristics by permanent magnet and magnetic barrier parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-SynRM) is a new type of motor that integrates the features of permanent magnet synchronous motor and synchronous reluctance motor. It has high efficiency, wide speed range, and low cost. Characteristics such as this have gained significant attention in domestic and international research recenly. In this article, a 550 W PMa-SynRM is taken as an example. The multilayer magnetic barrier structure on its rotor and the length and width of the permanent magnet are parametrized, and the effects of the parameters of the permanent magnet and the magnetic barrier on the average torque and torque ripple of the PMa-SynRM are investigated. The multi-objective global optimization of this motor is carried out by using the joint simulation method of Maxwell&Workbench& optiSLang, and the quadratic regression model of the high sensitivity parameters with the average torque, torque pulsation, and cogging torque is established, and finally, the final optimization result is selected in the set of optimal solutions of the Pareto frontier diagram on demand, and the correctness of the offered multi-objective optimization design method is verified by comparing the average torque, torque ripple and cogging torque of the original motor with that of the optimized.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Safe Navigation of UAVs Near High Voltage Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: High Voltage Transmission (Tx) line inspection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is rapidly increasing. Tx lines generate high Electric (E) and Magnetic (H) fields, leading to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) in UAV sensors. This paper focuses on predicting distance between Tx line and UAV during surveillance operations to navigate and operate UAVs drones safely. Various machine learning (ML) models such as Linear Regression, Random Forest Regression, Support Vector Regression, Decision Tree Regression, Gradient Boosting Regression, Multi Layer Perceptron Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors Regression are deployed to forecast the distance based on historical data. The study uses input features such as E-field, H-field, and Line Voltage rating, and the 3D distance between the Tx line and the UAV as target variable. Decision Tree Regression (DTR) model yielded the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 7.573 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 4.026 with a runtime of 0.998 ms.

articleTitle: The Little Network That Could: Adaptive Real-time Frequency Control in a 75+% Renewables Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The complications posed by renewable energy sources like wind and solar, paired with a growing influx of vehicle-to-grid batteries, have prompted enthusiasm for data-driven solutions surrounding frequency control, grid stabilization, and fault ride-through in modern power grids. The Matlabbased simulation landscape, however, lags far behind researcher interest. While many Simulink and Simscape models are available for grid scenarios with electronic converters that are PID controlled, it is nearly impossible to find even a single functioning model using ML/AI/Deep Learning architectures for converter or grid control of any sort – and equally difficult to find models suitable for adaptation to systems with 75+% RES penetration. This paper presents an entry point for future researchers: An AI-supported Virtual Inertia mechanism with continual realtime adaptation implemented in Simulink using the Matlab Deep Learning Toolbox. The data-driven component is designed to fill the role of PI and PID controllers, allowing all current failsafes and emergency shutoffs to remain in place. We demonstrate empirically in a scenario with varying wind speeds that an AI controller comprised of four neural network layers is able to outperform a classic PID controller in terms of battery SOC balanced against grid frequency. Critically, the AI controller and accompanying grid model are implemented without constant voltage or ideal current sources, making it one of the only open-source Matlab models suitable for forward research on adaptive grid control with high renewables penetration.

articleTitle: Research on the characteristics of hybrid excitation DC generator for vehicle based on field-circuit coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Hybrid excitation generator is the current research hotspot. This research studies a DC generator with hybrid excitation that has a tangential focused magnetic parallel structure. The working parameters of the system are introduced, and the principle of magnetic modulation is analyzed. The Maxwell2D and Simplorer field-circuit coupling model is built. The no-load characteristics are studied. The parameter selection of the relevant components in the filter circuit is discussed. The external characteristics are calculated, and the no-load air gap flux density and armature reaction air gap flux density are compared and analyzed. The simulation results show that the no-load characteristics and external characteristics of the generator reflect that the effect of applying positive excitation is better than that of negative excitation, which is suitable for low-speed and high-torque applications. When the load is constant, the filter capacitor value is $3 \mathrm{mF}-8 \mathrm{mF}$, and the inductance value is between $1 \mathrm{uH}-1 \mathrm{mH}$, the output DC voltage effect is better. After the armature reaction, the harmonic amplitude of the air gap flux density is smaller than that of the no-load air gap flux density, and the amplitude of the fundamental wave, 5P and 7P harmonics is smaller, and the amplitude of the 3P and 9P harmonics becomes larger. The adjustment range of the negative excitation stage is small, and the adjustment range of the positive excitation stage is large.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Mechanisms Behind Temperature-Dependent Impedance Behavior in Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells at High Current Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Positioning Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells (PEFCs) in the market depends on substantial advances that start from a deep knowledge concerning the influence of operating parameters, such as temperature-sweep and high-current density. In the present study, a comprehensive analysis of the impedance behavior of a single PEFC via Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out in order to unveil the mechanisms that impact the performance. The tests were setup using a high current density ($\mathbf{2. 0} \mathrm{A} \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) and in a wide temperature range ($40-90{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$). The impedance response, i.e., ohmic, charge, and mass transport resistances, were obtained using an equivalent circuit model that fits adequately. It was found that for temperatures below $70{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the loss due to ohmic resistance is dominant with a 54% contribution. In contrast, for temperatures above $70{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the loss due to charge transfer resistance became dominant, reaching a 72% contribution at $90{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, being the resistance most influenced when operating at high current load for a PEFC-type cell. Furthermore, empirical correlations were obtained to quantify the three internal resistances.

articleTitle: Research on PMSM Speed Control Based on Improved Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In order to enhance the dynamic response and disturbance rejection performance of permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) speed control system, this paper investigates an improved super-twisting sliding mode linear active disturbance rejection control strategy(ISTSM-LADRC). The sliding mode variable structure principle is employed to optimize the linear extended state observer(LESO) and linear state error feedback(LSEF) in the LADRC.Firstly, a super-twisting sliding mode LESO is designed to improve the observation performance of LESO in LADRC, enhancing the disturbance rejection capability of controller. Secondly, the super-twisting sliding mode control algorithm is employed to replace the original LSEF, improving the dynamic response of controller. Meanwhile, the hyperbolic tangent function ($\tanh$) is used to replace the sign function (sign) in the super-twisting sliding mode algorithm to further attenuate inherent sliding mode chattering, thus improving the stability of system. Next, the stability of the proposed control strategy is analyzed using Lyapunov theory.Finally, the feasibility of the control strategy is validated through Matlab/Simulink simulations. The simulation results demonstrate that the control strategy possesses better dynamic response performance and immunity compared to traditional LADRC and other controllers.

Author Keywords: Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Linear Extended State Observer

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Framework For An All Electric Hydrogen Powered Harbor Craft
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Green electrons have the potential to decarbonize the maritime industry which is faced with an existential challenge to reduce its emissions. Accounting for 3% of global emissions, marine vessels provide an all-important service to meet consumers’ transportation demands in the most cost-competitive manner. To realize any substantial reduction in maritime emissions, several actors need to come together to orchestrate this change. From ocean-going vessels to harbor crafts, they have different roles to play and are guided by their unique strengths and limitations. The maritime industry has a rich heritage of using mechanically driven engines to provide power and consequently, the use of electrons for main propulsion is relatively nascent. This paper considers the optimization-based strategy of a model predictive controller as part of the power management framework of a near-to-shore vessel, a hydrogen-powered all-electric tugboat. Power-sharing strategies are also discussed to ensure that the load is shared optimally between the fuel cells and batteries.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Floating Photovoltaic System in the Napique Lagoon to Evaluate the Supply of Electricity Demand in the District of Castilla, Piura
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Currently, there has been a significant increase in the installation of photovoltaic (PV) modules on water surfaces, due to the natural capacity of water to cool and keep the modules fresh, generating a reduction in the loss of thermal energy and avoiding the loss of efficiency due to overheating. However, in Peru the application of photovoltaic systems on floating surfaces is null and the studies published regarding their applications are limited so far. The objective of this research is to carry out a realistic simulation of a floating photovoltaic system driven by climate and based on energy demand in the district of Castilla. PVsystem and Global Solar atlas were used as calculation and simulation tools in this study. The results show that 1GWh is necessary to cover the electricity demand and that with the FPV around 76.28 MWh is produced, less than what is necessary per year with an average PR of 83.88%. The Ñapique lagoon is an ideal location for the implementation and installation of the FPV system because it covers 92.37% of the energy demand of the district of Castilla, which can be complemented with low requirements for a diesel generator.

articleTitle: Optimization Study on Dynamic Retrospective of Peaking Standby in Power Grids with High Percentage of New Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Both reliability and economy have an impact on the safe and stable operation of power systems. In the risk-optimized allocation model of peak standby within a single control window based on the economic cost-performance ratio sequential method of the improved control measures, a backtracking optimization algorithm for the start-stop path of peak standby in the full control cycle is proposed. Based on the optimized start-stop path scheme of the unit as the baseline path of the unit, the start-stop path of the peak standby unit at this position is backtracked and optimized to achieve the optimization objective of the optimal objective function for the full regulation cycle.

articleTitle: Modeling Emerging Uncertainties in Bulk Power System Reliability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Environmental concerns have led to increased deployment of clean and sustainable energy resources. Growing mix of emerging generation and transmission technologies, and increased uncertainty in load profiles at the various nodes of a bulk electric system network pose structural and operational complexities. Maintaining acceptable grid reliability has become increasingly challenging during system planning and operation. There is growing uncertainty in power supply due to rapid replacement of firm capacity by widely distributed intermittent renewable generation that are correlated by varying degrees. Moreover, emerging factors such as electric vehicles cause growing uncertainties in demand characteristics at the dispersed load points and create significant challenges in load modeling for composite system reliability (CSR) assessment. The adverse effects introduced by these emerging uncertainties can be mitigated using smart initiatives, such as demand response, energy storage, power electronic devices, and other smart grid technologies. This work investigates the development in modeling the characteristics of these new technologies and analyzes their utility in probabilistic CSR evaluation. The ongoing research in this direction is analyzed, and the research gaps are reported with a critical review in this paper.

articleTitle: Equal Transmission Power based Energy Efficient Wireless Sensor Networks for Industry 5.0
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The world today has progressed in science and technology to an extent unimagined by humans in the past. This scientific development has facilitated our lives in all aspects. All the sectors benefit from science. Industry 5, propelled by advanced automation and AI integration, revolutionizes manufacturing with unprecedented efficiency and customization. Sensors play a vital role in enabling Industry 5.0 by precise monitoring and analysis for informed decision-making. Due to the easiness of deployment, wireless sensor nodes are mostly used devices in the market. Energy consumption remains the primary limitation when these wireless sensors interact with one another in a network as they have a finite amount of energy to operate with—some may not even be rechargeable. In this paper, an energy-efficient algorithm is proposed after experimenting with several scenarios. When intermediary nodes are used as relays in place of direct contact with a remote node, transmission power is reduced. Relaying has the potential to increase energy efficiency in general. The analysis shows that the Equal Transmission Power (ETP) outperforms the other local algorithms.

articleTitle: Hosting Capacity Assessment of Residential Distribution Network for Growing Electric Vehicle Charging Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The widespread adoption of EVs will pose challenges to the planning and operation of the electric power grid if their charging is not coordinated and controlled. Therefore, the projection of EV load growth and hosting capacity analysis of EV charging infrastructure is critical for the power distribution grid. This study has investigated EV load projection in the state of North Dakota based on EV sales information, daily travel data, and temperature variations in North Dakota and investigated the load hosting capacity of a residential distribution system. An incremental hosting capacity analysis (HCA) was performed, and results show that the delayed/midnight charging strategy performs significantly better than the immediate/uncontrolled charging of EVs in the residential distribution grid. The addition of distributed generators with storage systems also improves the overall hosting capacity of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Temperature Control in A 3-Layer Insulating Neonatal Enclosure to Improve Thermal Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The World Health Organization mentions that the mortality of premature newborns varies widely between 10% and $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ depending on the country and economic income, observing that high-income countries have lower mortality rates in newborns born prematurely, due to access to advanced medical resources and better neonatal medical care infrastructure. Therefore, it is imperative to research and use current technology for the manufacture of affordable incubators in our country to save the lives of premature newborn babies. A new neonatal incubator system with three layers of insulation has been developed and patented in this research. Based on a 32-bit microcontroller AT91SAM3X8E of the Arduino Due module as the electronic system of the prototype and the RTD-PT1000 device was used to read the system. According to the protocol of the IEC 60601-2-19 standard, experimental tests for neonatal incubators were carried out. The methodology used for the analysis and evaluation made it possible to demonstrate the thermal efficiency in the prototype of three insulating layers by obtaining results with an error lower than those established by the standard.

articleTitle: Electro-mechanical Li-Ion Cell Model considering the composite Graphite-Silicon Structure of the negative Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To increase the volumetric energy density modern high-energy Lithium-Ion cells consist of Graphite/Silicon ($\mathbf{G r} / \mathbf{S i}$) composite negative electrodes. Due to the high volume expansion of up to 300% caused by (de)lithiation of Si, challenges arise by the usage of $\mathbf{G r} / \mathrm{Si}$-electrodes to prevent accelerated degradation. Therefore, accurate models to predict the cell expansion and pressure are of increasing interest. To investigate the mechanical behavior, half-cell Equivalent Circuit Models (ECMs) are coupled with a solid and liquid diffusion model in this article. The current density distribution among $\mathbf{S i}$ - and Gr -particles is determined by the assumption of an ideal parallel-connected of the active materials. An electrochemical dilatometer is used to measure the electrode expansion. Based on these measurements and literature values of volume changes of the crystal structure, changes of the pore volume are estimated. For the cell expansion and force development a visco-elastic model is implemented by using a spring in serial to a Kelvin-Voigt-Model. Simulations show high agreement with experimental data and literature values regarding cell voltage and expansion.
